title: Supporting coaches during games
summary: Use the matchday card while the coach leads.

sections.heading: Your outcome
sections.html:
Use the matchday card while the coach leads.

Estimated reading time; check at your own pace. This is developmental support, separate from qualifications and formal assessment.

sections.heading: Before kick-off
sections.html: Connect the match focus to practice. Agree what to observe, mentor location, quiet-prompt method and supervision duties. Choose whole-match support or a clearly timed window. Check local team-area eligibility, playing-time/substitution rules and emergency arrangements. A mentor without approved team-area access observes from a permitted location.

sections.heading: During play
sections.html: The coach leads and the mentor observes. Offer a brief quiet prompt only as agreed. Do not issue competing player instructions, argue with spectators or officials, or enter the field without authorisation. Safety overrides waiting for a debrief. Support an agreed duty only if it does not compromise supervision.

sections.heading: Half-time
sections.html: Water and recovery first. The coach leads. Share one useful observation and one achievable cue, with player input where appropriate. Recognise a purposeful attempt. Do not turn a short break into a second adult lecture or delay a restart.

sections.heading: After the final whistle
sections.html: Finish supervision and safe handover before an adult debrief, or agree a later conversation. No public critique. Capture one learning observation and one next-practice action. The score provides context; it is not the measure of mentoring success.

sections.heading: Illustrative staff-coach example
sections.html: Agree to observe tone, body language and intervention timing under pressure. After conceding, use the agreed quiet prompt. Recognise a brave decision even if possession was lost. Later compare one helpful intervention with a moment where silence would have helped. Keep this developmental conversation separate from formal performance assessment.

sections.heading: Practitioner guidance
sections.html: England Football: managing matchday and creating a great matchday experience provide practical guidance on player involvement, observation and adult behaviour. These are practitioner resources, not trials establishing programme effectiveness. Use the four-section blank matchday card in My mentoring → Field cards.

quiz.prompt: The team concedes. What should the mentor do?
options: Call different instructions over the coach.
Observe the pattern and offer only the agreed calm prompt.
quiz.explanation: Keep one clear adult lead; the score does not change the agreement.

quiz.prompt: Half-time is short. What takes priority?
options: Water, recovery and one useful message led by the coach.
A full tactical lecture from both adults.
Public criticism of the most recent mistake.
quiz.explanation: Recovery and one achievable cue protect a manageable player experience.

quiz.prompt: The mentor wants to change substitutions. What next?
options: Discuss with the responsible coach and follow local playing-time rules.
Use a practice bonus rule to change match eligibility.
quiz.explanation: Mentoring does not transfer team responsibility or override competition rules.

takeaway: Agree a matchday observation window and one calm prompt before kick-off.
